results.evidence: tests/test_log_reply.py, run with uv, passed 16/16. test_a_reply_is_recorded pins NOW=2026-12-01T00:00:00Z. It runs 'log-reply 1 interested --date 2026-11-30 --note "wants a call"'. It asserts exit 0, stdout 'reply recorded: lead 1 interested (activity N)', one reply activity with lead_id 1, and payload {type, received_on: 2026-11-30, note: wants a call}. test_every_reply_type_is_accepted covers all 7 types and each exits 0. 'log-reply 1 maybe' returns EXIT_USAGE, which is 2 (cli.py:39), because argparse rejects the choice, and nothing is appended. The implementation is send.log_reply in cottonwood/send.py and the CLI command in cottonwood/cli.py. I did not run the CLI by hand outside the tests.

log_reply in cottonwood/send.py inserts a reply activity. For opt_out it calls gate._insert_suppression(email_norm, 'opt-out reply to lead {lead_id}', 'log-reply', now) and then inserts a suppressed activity with contact_id. _insert_suppression returns the existing row without writing when the address is already suppressed. Reply.lines() prints 'suppressed: contact C' as the second line. The suppressed payload holds only reply_activity_id, source and added, so it has no email. tests/test_log_reply.py passed 16/16. Those tests cover each point of the AC: the Pat@Firm.example.com contact gets a suppression row with email_norm, reason and source as specified, the second stdout line is 'suppressed: contact 7', the reply and suppressed activities are appended with contact_id 7 and no '@' in the payload, an existing suppression row stays unchanged, and prepare-send afterwards is refused with the suppression check.

send.log_reply refuses an unknown lead with SendError('lead') and refuses opt_out/bounce with no contact email with SendError('contact'), both before BEGIN IMMEDIATE, so nothing is appended. For a bounce it inserts the reply activity, then calls eligibility._apply(..., INELIGIBLE, ...) in the same transaction. That call writes the eligibility_set activity. Reply.lines() adds EligibilityChange.line(), which formats 'contact C: eligibility eligible -> ineligible'. The CLI prints the errors as 'error: <what>: ...' and returns EXIT_REFUSED (1). tests/test_log_reply.py covers the bounce, the no-email refusal for opt_out and bounce on lead 2, and the unknown-lead refusal. They assert the exit codes, the stdout line, contacts.eligibility == ineligible, one reply and one eligibility_set activity, the stderr prefixes, and no activities appended. All 16 tests in the file passed.
